body_text: News Zenas BioPharma Submits Investigational New Dru... Zenas BioPharma Submits Investigational New Drug Application in China for ZB001 for the Treatment of Thyroid Eye Disease WALTHAM, Mass and SHANGHAI China, May 16, 2022 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Zenas BioPharma, a global biopharmaceutical company committed to becoming a leader in the development and commercialization of immune-based therapies for patients in need around the world, today announced the submission of an investigational new drug (IND) application to the China National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) for the initiation of a Phase 1/2 clinical study of ZB001 for the treatment of Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). This study is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy of ZB001. “The ZB001 IND submission to the NMPA marks a significant milestone for Zenas,” said Hua Mu, MD, PhD, Chief Executive Officer at Zenas. “There are currently no approved therapies for TED patients in China. Treatment options are limited and often involve high doses of steroids associated with serious side effects or surgical intervention. ZB001 has the potential to change the treatment paradigm for TED patients in China.” ZB001 is a differentiated humanized monoclonal antibody targeting insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R) for the treatment of TED. TED is a debilitating autoimmune disease that causes inflammation and fibrosis within the orbit of the eye, which can cause double vision, pain, and potential blindness. Patients with severe disease often require multiple remedial surgeries to the orbit, eye muscles, and eyelids. Zenas BioPharma licensed the exclusive rights to develop, manufacture and commercialize ZB001 (Viridian VRDN-001) and other compounds targeting IGF-1R in non-oncology indications in the greater area of China from Viridian Therapeutics, Inc. (Viridian) in October 2020. In October 2021, Viridian submitted an IND for VRDN-001 to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and in December 2021 initiated a Phase 1/2 clinical trial to evaluate proof of concept in TED patients in North America. About Zenas BioPharma Zenas BioPharma is a global biopharmaceutical company based in the USA and China committed to becoming a leader in the development and commercialization of immune-based therapies for patients in the US, China and around the world. Zenas is rapidly advancing a deep pipeline of innovative therapeutics that continues to grow through our successful business development strategy. Our experienced leadership team and network of business partners drive operational excellence to deliver potentially transformative therapies to improve the lives of those facing autoimmune and rare diseases. For more information about Zenas BioPharma, please visit www.zenasbio.com and follow us on Twitter at @ZenasBioPharma and LinkedIn . body_text: The claims brought by Genevant and Arbutus are unfounded because Moderna’s COVID-19 vaccine does not infringe any valid patents. Moderna quickly responded when the pandemic struck, swiftly developing, manufacturing, and providing doses of its COVID-19 vaccine to people around the world. ﻿ At this preliminary stage of the litigation, we have moved to dismiss plaintiffs’ claims relating to the sale of COVID-19 vaccine doses to the U.S. Government because plaintiffs have sued the wrong party in the wrong court. Under Federal law, claims against U.S. Government-contracted suppliers must proceed against the Government in the U.S. Court of Federal Claims. This law provides an important statutory protection for authorized government suppliers and played a critical role in encouraging companies, including Moderna, to step up and help the Government fight the COVID-19 pandemic. Ultimately, however, given that Moderna’s vaccine does not infringe any valid patents, plaintiffs’ claims will fail even if Arbutus and Genevant comply with the statutory requirements and refile in the Court of Federal Claims against the U.S. Government. title: At What Time of Day Is Your Phone Use the Worst?
summary: Our third installment of ClearSpace Stat of the Week mixes things up a little bit! Stat of the Week #1 showed how the hours saved by our…
body_text: Digital Addiction Phone Addiction Social Media Addiction Digital Wellness Digital Wellbeing At What Time of Day Is Your Phone Use the Worst? Wilson Barrett 3 min read · May 19, 2022 -- Press enter or click to view image in full size Our third installment of ClearSpace Stat of the Week mixes things up a little bit! Stat of the Week #1 showed how the hours saved by our users have accumulated over time, while Stat of the Week #2 depicted the differences across social media apps in how often people decide to actually use the app they opened after we encourage them to be intentional about their app use. This week’s stat is a little different because the information it provides is, frankly, unexpected. One of the bigger questions that we’ve had as a team is if there is a time of day when people most need a reminder to be intentional about their phone use. Many of the users we’ve talked to and other stories and experiences we’ve come across expressed an interest in reining in their phone use in one window of the day; often, people were most unsatisfied with how much they use their phones either first thing in the morning or just before they go to sleep at night. Get Wilson Barrett’s stories in your inbox Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer. Remember me for faster sign in The image below shows two sets of data: the percentage of intercepts where the user decides not to use the app they originally opened (blue) and the percentage of the day’s total intercepts during each hour (green), both broken down by the hour of the day in which they occur. Press enter or click to view image in full size Two of the three hours with the highest percentage non-use intercepts fall when users are most likely trying to fall asleep — 47.5% of intercepts in the 1 AM hour result in a non-use, as do 46.9% of intercepts in the 12 AM hour. Surprisingly, the second-highest hour for non-use intercepts comes in the middle of the day — 47.4% of intercepts in the 11 AM hour result in a non-use. On the other end of the spectrum, the three hours with the lowest non-use percentage are 5 AM (30.0%), 4 AM (35.4%), and 7 AM (63.7%). It’s hard to know for sure, but there are multiple possible reasons for this distribution of non-uses: intercepts in the morning are more likely to be part of a morning routine, intercepts at night might stem from reflexive restlessness instead of purposeful use, and a fresh stream of unseen content released overnight that users encounter during their first, and therefore more valuable, app use of the day. The green line shows that phone use (or at least, opens of apps connected to ClearSpace) is pretty consistent throughout the day, with each hour between 10 AM and 11 PM including between 5 and 7% of the day’s total intercepts. The top three hours by percent of the day’s opens are 9 PM, 8 PM, and 5 PM, while the three lowest hours are 4 AM, 3 AM, and 5 AM, respectively. title: Polycarbonate (PC): Definition, Properties, and Uses
summary: An overview of this useful group of thermoplastics
body_text: Polycarbonate (PC) is a high-performance thermoplastic polymer recognized for its strength, clarity, and resistance to high temperatures. Polycarbonate maintains impact resistance while remaining lightweight, making it suitable for demanding environments where toughness and visual clarity are required. The material’s durability supports long-term use in products (safety helmets, electronic device housings, and automotive interior components) that experience frequent handling or mechanical stress. PC plastic is used in eyewear lenses, automotive parts, electronic housings, safety shields, and optical media. The flexibility and stability under heat allow PC plastic to hold its shape without cracking. Its transparent surface provides clear visibility for protective covers and lenses. The combination of strength and versatility makes polycarbonate a dependable material across industrial, medical, and consumer applications. What is Polycarbonate (PC)? Polycarbonate (PC) is a thermoplastic polymer made through the step-growth polymerization of bisphenol A (BPA) and phosgene. PC is known for its combination of strength, transparency, and heat resistance, giving it a balance of toughness and lightweight performance. Polycarbonate maintains excellent dimensional stability and resists impact without cracking, even under stress or fluctuating temperatures. These characteristics make it suitable for producing durable products (automotive parts, eyewear lenses, and electronic housings). PC material is valued for its clarity and electrical insulation properties, making it practical for industrial and consumer applications where insulation is required. The ability to withstand high temperatures while retaining form and strength ensures long-term reliability in demanding environments. The material’s versatility has made polycarbonate an essential choice in industries (automotive manufacturing, electronics, construction, and medical equipment production) that require precision, durability, and safety in product design. An example of polycarbonate 3D printed by Xometry How is PC Material Made PC Material is made by reacting bisphenol A (BPA) with phosgene gas in a controlled chemical reaction (polycarbonate polymerization), forming long molecular chains that provide the material with strength, clarity, and heat resistance. The process forms long molecular chains that give the material its strength, clarity, and resistance to heat. Understanding how polycarbonate is made begins with the two main substances (bisphenol A and phosgene gas) reacting in a controlled environment to create a molten polymer, which is then cooled and shaped into pellets for further manufacturing. Polycarbonate (PC) is produced using interfacial polymerization of bisphenol A and phosgene. Ziegler-Natta and metallocene catalysts are used for olefin polymerization, not for PC production. The catalyst systems used in polymerization (polypropylene and polyethylene) influence the molecular structure and final properties of the polymer, affecting its flexibility, impact strength, and thermal stability. The precise process by which Polycarbonate achieves its toughness and clarity makes it ideal for electronic components, safety equipment, and optical lenses. What is the PC Material Full Form? The PC Material Full Form is Polycarbonate, a durable and transparent thermoplastic polymer widely used in various industries. The PC full form refers to a material known for its strength, impact resistance, and heat tolerance, making it dependable for demanding applications. The polycarbonate full form is recognized and used in manufacturing products (automotive parts, electronic housings, safety helmets, and optical lenses). Its toughness and clarity allow it to replace glass and metal in different designs, offering lightweight performance with long-lasting durability. What Are the Main Challenges in Manufacturing PC Plastic? The main challenges in manufacturing PC Plastic are listed below. High Production Cost: The production of polycarbonate requires expensive raw materials (bisphenol A and phosgene). The complex chemical processes needed to synthesize PC contribute to the higher cost compared to other plastics. Environmental Concerns: The production process for polycarbonate involves hazardous chemicals (phosgene), which pose environmental and safety risks if not properly managed. The production process presents challenges in ensuring safe production methods and mitigating environmental impact regarding the use of hazardous chemicals (phosgene). Processing Complexity: Polycarbonate requires precise control of temperature and pressure during molding and extrusion. Large-scale production of polycarbonate is challenging because even slight variations in temperature, pressure, or material formulation lead to defects or inconsistent material properties. How Does Polycarbonate Plastic Affect the Quality of Products? Polycarbonate plastic affects the quality of products by improving their strength, impact resistance, and visual clarity. The material’s toughness prevents cracking or breaking under stress, making it reliable for use in eyewear lenses, automotive parts, and electronic housings. Polycarbonate plastic maintains its clarity and shape even under extreme temperatures or cold, ensuring consistent performance in various environments. Polycarbonate plastic combines durability with transparency, long-lasting, high-quality products that retain their appearance and functionality over time. What Are the Advantages of Polycarbonate Plastic? The advantages of Polycarbonate Plastic are listed below. Strength and Durability: Polycarbonate offers exceptional impact resistance, making it suitable for protective applications (safety glasses and automotive parts). Strength enables polycarbonate plastic to withstand significant stress without breaking, making it a preferred material for high-demand environments. Transparency: The high optical clarity is one of the advantages of polycarbonate, making it ideal for use in products (eyewear lenses, skylights, and windows). It offers crystal-clear visibility while maintaining the durability of plastic. Heat Resistance: Polycarbonate's ability to withstand high temperatures makes it an ideal material for use in industrial settings, where it must endure heat without degrading. Stability and structural integrity are maintained even in demanding applications. What Are the Disadvantages of Polycarbonate Plastic? The disadvantages of Polycarbonate Plastic are listed below. Scratching: Polycarbonate is highly susceptible to surface scratches, which can significantly impact its transparency. Coatings enhance scratch resistance, but the material remains susceptible to wear in certain applications. Polycarbonate tends to lose clarity due to surface scratches; however, it maintains high optical clarity and is commonly used for optical lenses and transparent panels. Scratch-resistant coatings help maintain their appearance over time. Environmental Impact: Polycarbonate is not biodegradable and contributes to long-term environmental pollution. Its disposal and accumulation in landfills add to the global plastic waste problem, as polycarbonate does not break down naturally. High Cost: The production of polycarbonate is more expensive compared to other common plastics (polyethylene or polypropylene) due to the raw materials and processing complexity involved. The higher cost of polycarbonate limits its use in applications where budget constraints are a priority, when other plastics provide similar performance at a lower price. What Are the Properties of Polycarbonate? The properties of polycarbonate include high impact resistance, optical clarity, dimensional stability, heat resistance, and electrical insulation. The material is not considered the most suitable for high-voltage electrical insulation compared to other materials. The material is known for its ability to withstand extreme temperatures and resist cracking under stress, making it ideal for use in applications that require durability (eyewear lenses and automotive parts). PC material properties include excellent toughness, lightweight characteristics, and high transparency, which contribute to its versatility in manufacturing and engineering applications. Polycarbonate is a good electrical insulator, making it suitable for many electrical and electronic applications. It is not ideal for high-voltage insulation compared to other materials (silicone rubber and epoxy resins). Its strength and flexibility, combined with its resistance to environmental stress, ensure that polycarbonate remains a reliable material across a wide range of industries. What is the Density of Polycarbonate? The density of polycarbonate ranges from 1.20 to 1.22 grams per cubic centimeter (g/cm³), depending on the formulation. The range of density contributes to the material's combination of strength and durability while keeping it relatively lightweight. The density of polycarbonate contributes to its resistance to impacts and ability to endure harsh environments without adding excess weight. These characteristics make it an ideal material for use in different industries (automotive, electronics, and construction). The density of PC ensures that polycarbonate maintains its shape and integrity under stress, providing lasting performance in various applications. Polycarbonate is lightweight and easy to handle, making it a popular choice for components requiring toughness and practical usability. The balance of properties enables its use in everything from eyewear lenses to bulletproof windows. What is the Softening Temperature of Polycarbonate? The softening temperature of polycarbonate is typically around 150–160°C, and its glass transition temperature is approximately 145–150°C. The high melting point of polycarbonate makes it an ideal material for applications in environments where exposure to high temperatures is inevitable. It enables polycarbonate to maintain its structural integrity and performance in demanding conditions, such as those found in the automotive, electronics, and engineering industries. The PC melting point is a key factor that contributes to the material's versatility. Polycarbonate's ability to withstand high temperatures without deforming is crucial for components such as headlamp lenses and interior panels in automotive applications. It is used for housings of devices that require heat resistance in electronics, ensuring that the material maintains its form and function even under extended exposure to heat. What is the Chemical Formula of Polycarbonate? The chemical formula of polycarbonate is (C15H16O2)n, where n represents the number of repeating units in the polymer chain formed from bisphenol A (BPA) and phosgene. The formula reflects the molecular structure of polycarbonate, which consists of bisphenol A (BPA) and phosgene. The reaction between these two substances forms a repeating unit that gives polycarbonate its robust properties. The polycarbonate chemical formula and its resulting polymer structure contribute to the material's strength, transparency, and high-impact resistance. The PC polymer formula provides polycarbonate with excellent durability, making it ideal for applications like eyewear lenses, automotive parts, and electronic devices. The strength and stability of the polymer chain are crucial for maintaining its performance in harsh conditions, including exposure to high temperatures and UV radiation. What is the Structure of Polycarbonate? The structure of polycarbonate is defined by its linear arrangement, consisting of repeating units derived from bisphenol A (BPA) and phosgene, where the ester linkages connect the monomers in the polymer backbone. The polymer structure forms long chains that provide polycarbonate with its strong and durable properties. The monomers BPA and phosgene are linked through ester bonds, creating a polymer backbone that gives polycarbonate its characteristic strength. The rigid structure formed by the aromatic rings in the polymer enhances the material’s resistance to impact and heat, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. The PC polymer structure contributes to polycarbonate's unique balance of strength and flexibility. The inclusion of aromatic rings in the molecular structure is a key factor in its ability to withstand stress without breaking. The design allows polycarbonate to maintain high transparency, excellent dimensional stability, and resistance to UV degradation. Polycarbonate is commonly used in areas such as eyewear lenses, optical discs, and protective coverings. What is Polycarbonate Used for? Polycarbonate is used for eyewear lenses, automotive parts, electronic housings, medical devices, safety helmets, and optical media (CDs and DVDs). Polycarbonate’s high impact resistance prevents cracking, while its amorphous structure provides optical clarity suitable for lenses and protective covers. Understanding what polycarbonate is used for reveals its heat stability and durability, which support long-term performance in applications subject to repeated stress or frequent use. Polycarbonate applications extend to construction glazing, machine guards, and lighting covers, where both strength and transparency are required simultaneously. The material retains its shape under pressure and temperature changes, ensuring reliable function and appearance across both industrial and consumer applications. What is Polycarbonate Material Used for in Medical Applications? Polycarbonate Material is used in Medical Applications for producing diagnostic equipment housings, sterilizable containers, and non-invasive surgical instrument components. The high impact strength prevents breakage during handling, while its clarity supports accurate visual inspection during medical procedures. Polycarbonate’s resistance to heat and chemicals enables repeated sterilization by methods such as ethylene oxide (EtO) and gamma radiation; however, frequent autoclaving can cause degradation over time. The biocompatibility and durability of polycarbonate material make it suitable for medical housings, protective shields, and precision components used in patient care environments. Can Polycarbonate be Used in Medical Implants? No, Polycarbonate cannot be used in medical implants (temporary orthopedic supports) due to limited long-term biocompatibility and potential degradation in the body. Polycarbonate’s strength and durability make it suitable for rigid protective medical housings and face shields, but not for direct-contact orthopedic devices such as splints or braces. Polycarbonate’s lightweight nature, transparency, and impact resistance make it practical for temporary non-implantable medical applications (diagnostic equipment covers or face shields). It is preferred in situations where a strong, durable, and easily sterilizable material is required, but permanent implantation is not necessary. What Are the Applications of PC Material in Construction? The applications of PC material in construction are listed below. Roofing Materials: Polycarbonate is used in roofing materials for greenhouses and translucent roofing systems, due to its strength, impact resistance, and ability to withstand harsh weather conditions. It provides a durable, lightweight solution for translucent roofing or skylight systems in structures exposed to extreme temperatures or storms. Insulation: Polycarbonate is used in insulating glazing systems or thermal barriers in windows and facades, but it is not commonly used as an insulation material itself due to its relatively high thermal conductivity. Polycarbonate in insulating glazing systems or windows helps improve energy efficiency by providing thermal resistance and reducing heat loss. Window and Glazing: Polycarbonate is used in window and glazing applications due to its impact resistance and ability to transmit light effectively. PC is used for skylights, safety windows, and facades, providing clarity and protection from external impacts. What Role Does PC Plastic Play in Automotive Safety Features? The role that PC Plastic plays in Automotive Safety features is listed below. Airbags: Polycarbonate is used in airbag covers and housing components due to its strength and impact resistance. However, other materials, such as nylon, are typically used in the inflation system. Safety Glazing: Polycarbonate is used in automotive windows, roof panels, and safety shields due to its impact resistance. However, windshields are typically made from laminated glass for improved clarity and scratch resistance. The material provides additional protection, reducing the risk of breakage during collisions and helping protect passengers from flying debris. Interior Components: Polycarbonate is commonly used in vehicle dashboards and other interior components due to its exceptional durability. It is resistant to wear and tear from daily use, ensuring that interior parts maintain their appearance and functionality over time. What Are the Benefits of PC Plastic in Food Packaging? The benefits of PC Plastic in food packaging are listed below. Non-Toxic: Polycarbonate is approved for food contact in specific applications and grades, but its BPA content must be carefully controlled, as BPA is a concern in food-related packaging. Ensure BPA-free polycarbonate is used for food packaging applications. The certification for BPA-free polycarbonate ensures that the material does not release harmful chemicals, making it a reliable choice for specific food packaging applications. Durability: Polycarbonate offers excellent moisture resistance and the ability to withstand a wide range of temperatures. The material is ideal for food packaging because it protects contents against spoilage during transportation or storage. Cost-Effective: Polycarbonate is affordable compared to other high-performance plastics ( Polyether Ether Ketone, Polyphenylene Sulfide, Polytetrafluoroethylene) used in food packaging. Polycarbonate is more affordable than higher-performance plastics (PEEK, PPS, and PTFE), though it is more expensive than other commonly used food packaging materials (PET and HDPE). What is the Cost of Polycarbonate Plastic Compared to Other Plastics? The Cost of Polycarbonate Plastic is higher compared to other plastics (polyethylene and polypropylene), because its production process and high-performance characteristics require more precise control during manufacturing. Polycarbonate plastic’s greater strength, clarity, and heat resistance justify the added expense in applications where durability and safety are paramount, such as protective equipment, automotive components, and optical devices. Long service life and low breakage risk make it a valuable investment, despite its initial cost. How is Polycarbonate Plastic Recycled? Polycarbonate Plastic is recycled using mechanical processes, which involve shredding the material into small pieces, melting, and reforming it into new products. Chemical recycling is less commonly used for polycarbonate due to its complexity and cost. The mechanical process involves grinding the material into small pieces, which are then melted and reformed into new products. Chemical recycling breaks down polycarbonate into its basic components (bisphenol A and phosgen), but the process is more complex and less commonly used compared to mechanical recycling. Polycarbonate is reprocessed into products (safety barriers and optical lenses), but high-quality recycled material is required for optical applications due to performance and clarity requirements. It enables the continued use of the material, reducing waste and promoting sustainability in industries that rely on polycarbonate’s durability and transparency. Is Polycarbonate (PC) More Biodegradable than Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS)? No, Polycarbonate (PC) is not more biodegradable than Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS). The materials are synthetic plastics designed to be durable and resistant to environmental degradation. However, PC tends to degrade faster than ABS under certain environmental conditions (exposure to UV light and weathering). The degradation of PC leads to the material breaking down into smaller fragments over time. ABS remains more stable and resistant to weather-related wear. The environmental impact of Polycarbonate (PC) and Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) materials is significant, as they contribute to long-term plastic pollution. PC and ABS require proper disposal and recycling efforts to mitigate their impact on ecosystems. Does Polycarbonate (PC) Have Better Acoustic Properties than High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) has better acoustic properties than High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) due to its higher density, which helps it absorb vibrations and reduce sound transmission more effectively. PC offers superior sound insulation and noise-dampening characteristics due to its higher density and ability to absorb vibrations more effectively, making it ideal for applications where noise reduction is a priority (soundproofing materials and acoustic panels). HDPE is lighter and less effective at blocking sound, making it less suitable for acoustic purposes. Polycarbonate (PC) is commonly used for applications (acoustic panels, soundproof windows, and noise barriers) in which sound reduction is needed, and High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) is used for applications (storage tanks, pipes, and protective covers) in which impact resistance and chemical resistance are required. Is Polycarbonate (PC) Easier to Recycle than Polyethylene (PE)? Yes, Polyethylene (PE) is easier to recycle than polycarbonate (PC), primarily due to PE's simpler chemical structure and established recycling infrastructure. PE is widely accepted by recycling facilities, making Polyethylene (PE ) easier to process and reuse. Recycling PC presents challenges, such as contamination and the complexity of its chemical composition, which complicates the separation and purification process required for effective recycling. Does Polycarbonate (PC) Offer Better Gloss Retention than High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) offers better gloss retention than High Impact Polystyrene (HIPS) due to its superior durability and resistance to surface degradation, even under exposure to UV light and environmental stress. PC maintains its glossy finish longer, even under exposure to UV light and environmental stress. High-Impact Polystyrene (HIPS) tends to degrade more quickly, leading to a loss of its glossy appearance. Gloss retention is essential in consumer electronics and automotive parts, where a polished and durable surface contributes to the overall aesthetic and perceived quality of the product. To learn more, see our full guide on High-Impact Polystyrene (HIPS) . Is Polycarbonate (PC) More Resistant to Gas Permeation than Polylactic Acid (PLA)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) is more resistant to gas permeation than Polylactic Acid (PLA). PC offers superior resistance to gases, making it a better choice for applications that require airtight seals, such as food and beverage packaging. The reduced permeability helps maintain the quality and shelf life of products by preventing the intrusion of oxygen, which leads to spoilage or degradation. Polylactic Acid (PLA) is biodegradable and eco-friendly, but it does not provide the same level of gas barrier properties as polycarbonate, making it less suitable for packaging applications that require extended freshness. Does Polycarbonate (PC) Have Better Transparency for Optical Applications than Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) has better transparency for optical applications than Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET). PC offers good transparency and is used in eyewear lenses, and Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) is preferred for high-precision optical applications due to its better clarity. The material’s ability to transmit light without distortion is vital in optical applications, as even slight imperfections affect vision and the performance of optical devices. Polycarbonate (PC) is less commonly used for high-precision optical products due to its lower optical clarity compared to Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) , which offers superior transparency for demanding optical applications. Is Polycarbonate (PC) More Cost-Effective for Low-Volume Manufacturing than Nylon (PA)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) is more cost-effective for low-volume manufacturing than Nylon (PA). The processing of PC is simpler and requires less specialized equipment, which reduces the overall manufacturing cost. Low-volume industries (medical device manufacturing, custom electronics, and specialty automotive parts) must consider material costs when making production decisions, as cheaper materials (PC) help maintain cost efficiency. The Nylon (PA) offers high strength and wear resistance, but its higher cost and more complex processing make it less common for low-volume production, where cost control is crucial. However, it remains a viable option for applications where performance is a top priority. Does Polycarbonate (PC) Have Better Dimensional Tolerance than Polybutylene Terephthalate (PBT)? No, Polycarbonate (PC) does not have better dimensional tolerance than Polybutylene Terephthalate (PBT). PBT provides higher dimensional stability due to its lower moisture absorption and consistent thermal behavior during molding. Maintaining precise dimensional tolerances is essential in injection molding, as it affects part alignment, fit, and long-term performance in assembled products. The Polybutylene Terephthalate (PBT) is preferred for high-precision applications, such as electrical connectors and automotive components, where exact dimensions are required. Is Polycarbonate (PC) More Easily Fabricated than Acetal (POM)? Yes, Polycarbonate (PC) is more easily fabricated than Acetal (POM). Polycarbonate (PC) is easier to form and mold due to its flexibility, but Acetal (POM) offers better machinability because of its hardness and low-friction properties that allow for cleaner cutting and tighter tolerances. Acetal (POM) typically results in faster machining, less tool wear, and better dimensional accuracy than Polycarbonate (PC). PC is more advantageous in forming and molding, where its ease of thermoforming reduces cycle times. The Acetal (POM) does not increase tool wear, as it is considered one of the most machinable engineering plastics, offering smooth cutting, low friction, and shorter fabrication times compared to Polycarbonate (PC). title: After Regaining Popularity, Boxing Is Here To Stay
summary: The sport of boxing is bringing spectators to the ring once again, and this time to a fan base who are gloving up and hitting the punching bag themselves.
body_text: Boxing has seen a huge rise in popularity with both casual and hardcore fans flocking to the sport in huge numbers. Gen Z is showing up to watch fights and adding boxing workouts to their fitness regimen. In fact, according to a 2021 Harris Poll , boxing is currently the 4th most popular sport in the United States, and according to Luker on Trends, boxing was the fastest growing sport between 2010-2020. But what is driving this sudden return to the boxing ring? Well, there are a lot of factors to consider. Boxing Has Incredible Narrative Strength Boxing isn’t simply about two fighters hitting each other – it always has a story to it. Whether that story is Canelo Alvarez rising from poverty to become the greatest boxer in the world or Floyd Mayweather going undefeated in 50 professional fights, boxing has a narrative presence that makes it easy to market, especially to new younger fans. According to Top Rank CRO Brian Kelly , a big part of boxing’s recent popularity surge is the large presence it has on social media and streaming outlets, like YouTube, Instagram, and Twitter. These social media platforms allow incredible highlight reels and video content that is marketable to millions of fans, especially Gen Zers, drawing them to the sport. Sensational Exhibitions It is impossible to overestimate the impact the Paul Brothers have had on the sport of boxing. Now, I’m sure I’ve already made several boxing purists reading this upset by saying that, but just hear me out. It is undeniable that Jake and Logan Paul have a huge draw with Generation Z audiences, and that their antics sell tickets. And we can infer from the poll data and the fact that boxing is growing despite the Paul Brothers having not fought in quite a while, that many of those fans who originally only came to see the Paul Brothers are sticking around and seeing everything the combat sport has to offer, even dipping their toes into the water and deciding to get some boxing training themselves! Boxing Training Fits The Modern Lifestyle While boxing as entertainment has seen a surge in popularity, it's no longer just a spectator sport, as boxing and kickboxing workouts are also at an all time high. The truth is, the way MMA fighters and pro boxers train is an ideal workout routine for the modern lifestyle. Before the pandemic, there were more boxing and kickboxing gyms than spin studios and now, as most American adults don’t have time to drive to a traditional gym every day, boxing and MMA-style workouts can easily be done from home with proper guidance from a professional instructor online. More importantly, this type of training is never, ever boring! Hitting a punching bag or learning footwork is always an engaging way to work on both cardio and muscle definition at the same time, and you can finish your workout in as little as 30 minutes. Boxing Is Here To Stay Boxing has never been a fad, and both it and Mixed Martial Arts are continuing to rise in popularity. The stories, the highlight reels, and the atmosphere of a boxing or MMA match can’t be equaled by any other sport. All of that combined with how easy it is for anybody to pick up a pair of boxing gloves , sign up for FightCamp, and learn real boxing techniques taught by professional fighters, create a sport that is by everyone, for everyone. So don’t call it a comeback, boxing is here to stay. Are you ready to train like a fighter? Get access to hundreds of boxing, kickboxing, strength, conditioning, recovery, and stretching workouts that will push you mentally and physically. Download the FREE FightCamp App and train with real fighters from the comfort of your own home.

title: Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. Announces New 120 Megawatt Bitcoin Mining Facility in Texas, USA
summary: Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. is pleased to announce a new 120 megawatt Bitcoin mining facility in Texas, USA.
body_text: Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. Announces New 120 Megawatt Bitcoin Mining Facility in Texas, USA New Texas Bitcoin mining facility expected to be fully operational in Q4, 2022 Sydney , Australia and New York City, USA — May 16th, 2022 — Mawson Infrastructure Group Inc. (NASDAQ:MIGI) (“Mawson”), a digital infrastructure provider, is pleased to announce it will develop a new 120 Megawatt (MW) Bitcoin mining facility in Texas, USA. Mawson, through its wholly owned subsidiary Luna Squares Texas LLC, has signed leases with 5 year terms, including 2 options to extend by a further 5 years, for a total of 15 years. The combined facility consists of 4 individual sites in close proximity to one another. On-site development is expected to commence in Q2, 2022, with the facility becoming fully operational in Q4, 2022. Based on utilization of current generation Bitcoin mining ASIC hardware, this new facility could potentially accommodate up to 4.0 Exahash (EH) of Bitcoin mining operational capacity. Mawson intends to utilize both Carbon Credits and Renewable Energy Credits (REC’s) for this facility, as well as to participate in curtailment programs to ensure our Net Zero Carbon and strong ESG focus is maintained. The sites have been selected due to the substantial local infrastructure already available to Mawson. Mawson is now working to secure Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) required to commission the facility and will update stockholders on this front in due course. Mawson has collaborated with JAI Energy and Texas Pacific Land Corporation (NYSE:TPL) on the project, both of which will share in the revenue streams generated by the project, as well as have an option to acquire an equity interest in Luna Squares Texas LLC. Texas Pacific Land Corporation, one of the largest landowners in the State of Texas, is the landlord of two of the sites. The other two sites are situated on family-owned private lands. James Manning, CEO and Founder of Mawson , said, "Texas is rapidly emerging as an exciting new Bitcoin mining province in the United States, and thus we are excited to have established an initial foothold in the state. In an environment where energy and energy infrastructure are in high demand, we are looking forward to beginning on-ground civil works near-term. Community engagement is an important priority for Mawson, and we look forward to working closely with the local counties and continuing to be a great corporate citizen in the communities in which we operate. We are excited to have collaborated with JAI Energy, and Texas Pacific Land Corporation - one of the largest landowners in the State of Texas with approximately 880,000 acres of land. We are looking forward to civil works beginning on our first site in Texas and exploring the substantial opportunities these new relationships bring Mawson Infrastructure Group.” Justin Ballard, CEO and Co-Founder of JAI Energy , said, " Mawson is one of the premier operators in the Bitcoin mining industry and we are excited to expand JAI Energy’s presence into Texas with them. We identified Mawson early on as an ideal partner due to their reputation, operational excellence and culture. We know the West Texas community will welcome Mawson and we are proud to have played a role in bringing them to the great State of Texas and further establishing Texas as the Bitcoin mining capital. Additionally, it is extremely valuable to the entire Bitcoin mining space to see a group like TPL getting involved in the industry. JAI Energy has continually strived to educate energy companies and landowners on the benefits that Bitcoin mining can bring and we applaud TPL for being a leader and jumping at the opportunity to enter this emerging industry.” Tyler Glover, CEO of Texas Land Corporation, Ballard, CEO and Co-Founder of JAI Energy , said, “This project marks the beginning of TPL’s journey into Bitcoin, and we are fortunate to collaborate with Mawson and JAI as two highly regarded companies in the bitcoin mining industry. We believe TPL’s extensive surface footprint in West Texas can serve as a premier destination for the Bitcoin mining industry, providing site locations proximate to existing grid infrastructure and excellent solar and wind resource for future renewable power procurement. We are aligned to see this venture succeed and scale as we look to leverage our unique asset base, industry and customer relationships, and the region’s energy abundance. For TPL, our shareholders will benefit from a unique royalty stream while retaining an option to participate as an equity partner.” About Mawson Infrastructure Mawson Infrastructure Group (NASDAQ: MIGI) is a digital infrastructure provider, with multiple operations throughout the USA and Australia. Mawson’s vertically integrated model is based on a long-term strategy to promote the global transition to the new digital economy. title: Celebrating Clinical Trials Day
summary: SOPHiA GENETICS is excited to celebrate Clinical Trials Day. This blog dives a little deeper into the history of clinical trials and how they continue to advance healthcare. The post Celebrating Clinical Trials Day appeared first on SOPHiA GENETICS .
body_text: Some History Around This Date Clinical Trials Day, May 20th, brings awareness to clinical trials, but most importantly it celebrates and recognizes the people who run clinical trials and their contribution towards improving health. May 20th marks the anniversary of what is considered to be the first randomized clinical trial, performed in 1747 by James Lind1. He conducted a controlled clinical trial that compared six treatments for scurvy in 12 sailors with scurvy who all lived in the same quarters and had the same diet. He was able to identify that the two men who were treated with fresh citrus had the most positive results, however he never concretely recommended this treatments as a cure for scurvy and continued to find other remedies since fresh citrus was in limited supply. Lind is recognized for his experimental methods when conducting this study, attempting to compare similar subjects, thus reducing confounding variables2. You can learn more about James Lind and his achievements here . Clinical Trials Today: impacting lives in the precision medicine era Clinical trials today have obviously advanced way beyond this approach; however, we can still see how trials are rooted in Lind’s work, analyzing different treatments to identify their effects on a disease. Clinical trial work today is not only more advanced but being conducted on a much larger scale and across the world. Since 1999 over 671,000 clinical trials have been registered with the World Health Organization , with just under 60,000 being registered in 2021 alone. These trials increase access and knowledge of experimental treatments. Currently, there are around 4,000 active trials that are using targeted biomarkers associations for oncology. To truly test the efficacy and effectiveness of these drugs, it is imperative to find patients with compatible biomarker signatures for the treatment. As diagnostic testing advances, these biomarker signatures can become more and more specific. Running these clinical trials would not be possible without the clinical research professionals that support them. These individuals work across a variety of functions and to maintain the integrity of the research through a wide range of duties including data collection, recruitment, development of documentation, education and so much more. We at SOPHiA GENETICS are happy to take time to recognize these individuals and we thank them for all they do to advance research, medicine, and care. SOPHiA GENETICS Helps Sites Gather and Analyze Multimodal Data in their Population of Interest In one of our ongoing clinical studies in lung cancer, the DEEP-Lung-IV study, we aim to leverage deep learning-enabled analysis to aggregate multimodal data (e.g., clinical, biological, genomic, and radiomics data) to identify and validate predictive signatures associated with response to immunotherapy and prognosis of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. This international and multicentric project addresses an important translational research question in a pragmatic way. Our collective intelligence receives many negative or positive predictive signals (clinical, imaging and molecular signals) in this area, yet it is currently unable to integrate them in an intelligible way. The goal of the DEEP-Lung-IV project is to integrate all these individual, discrete predictive signals into an artificial intelligence-based framework to enable us to make this information intelligible and thus allow us to intelligently choose the first line of treatment for our patient s. Pr. Jacques Cadranel, Sorbonne Université and AP-HP Hôpital Tenon – Paris, France SOPHiA GENETICS Supports Clinical Trial Recruitment with SOPHiA DDM Trial Match. Accelerate biomarker-driven participant recruitment, even in rare biomarker cohorts with SOPHiA DDM Trial Match. This real-time site and patient identification analytical solution enables you to optimize clinical trial site selection ahead of clinical trial set up and supports your trial rescue strategy by finding additional centers for ongoing trials not meeting recruitment goals. Learn more about how SOPHiA DDM Trial Match can support identifying your targeted trial population. References “Clinical Trials Day.” Clinical Trials Day, https://www.clinicaltrialsday.org/#clinical-trials-day. Milne, Iain. “Who Was James Lind, and What Exactly Did He Achieve.” Journal of the Royal Society of Medicine, vol. 105, no. 12, 2012, pp. 503–508., https://doi.org/10.1258/jrsm.2012.12k090. title: Hyperautomation and AI Agents in 2022 [2023 update]
summary: Hyperautomation is one of the latest technology trends that businesses are scrambling to keep up with. What is it and how will it affect the business landscape in the coming years?
body_text: In this age of technology, businesses are constantly looking for ways to gain an edge over the competition with the use of the latest innovations. Today, transforming manual functions into automated processes has become the norm. Businesses are opting to save on costs and invest in the future through automation. What is hyperautomation? Hyperautomation is one of the emerging strategic technology trends in 2022. The IT research firm Gartner first coined the term in 2019. Hyperautomation refers to the use of robotic process automation (RPA) combined with machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI). The result? Even more automated automation with the goal of improving business workflow and efficiency. Data engineers play a huge role in the development of AI. Most businesses today have their own team of engineers to further automate already existing business processes. With hyperautomation, even the processes that previously needed experts to complete can now be done using robotic process automation and artificial intelligence. Arguably the biggest advantage of using hyperautomation is that it not only speeds up work – it makes it more efficient. ‍ AI Agents in Hyperautomation AI Agents are commonly seen in business processes and workflows. These assistants display a high level of versatility as they can interact with customers and employees alike. Common examples of AI Agents include website chatbots and virtual executive assistants such as Siri for iOS devices and Cortana for Windows. These AI Agents are a result of automation with the use of ML and AI. AI Agents already help improve business processes. These assistants can engage all stakeholders in the business and create a dynamic workflow. But what happens when AI Agents undergo hyperautomation? Hyperautomation transforms and improves AI Agents. It can create a more powerful version of the AI Agent with the combination of RPA and machine learning. The AI Agents become a better version of themselves – more engaging, more efficient, and more knowledgeable. Through hyperautomation, specific data that used to be processed manually can be automated – even complex data that could only be processed by experts. In essence, hyperautomation upskills the AI Agent. Just like how employees are trained and upskilled by their companies, AI Agents can absorb and learn new skills and knowledge with the use of hyperautomation. The result is a team of AI Agents that serve as a digital workforce. These assistants can seamlessly connect various business processes, analyze more complex data, make decisions, and efficiently perform repetitive tasks. Currently, applications of hyperautomation in AI Agents are found in several industries. There is AI in the beauty industry , retail and trading, healthcare, banking and finance, and in several other industries. The AI Agents in these industries work on creating a customized profile for each client so they can offer the best products and services of the business. ‍ Building a Future with Hyperautomation As more businesses are joining the trend of hyperautomation, what does this mean for the future? The goal of hyperautomation is to replace current business processes done by employees. Instead of wasting the precious time of an employee doing processes such as onboarding new hires or consulting for specific fields, the use of hyperautomation can transform these processes into automated programs. Hyperautomation also aids in data privacy and security , as well as in preventing data loss. Thus, more employees can focus on their specific roles within the business instead of spending time doing tasks that can be done by an AI Agent. Counterproductivity and inefficiency can easily be eliminated with the use of hyperautomation. The future of the business sector becomes brighter with hyperautomation. Big businesses are now competing to develop their own hyperautomation systems that will replace already outdated workplace practices. From the previous learnings from AI and automation, hyperautomation takes things a step further by interlinking all these automated processes. This will lead to a highly efficient business that will remain competitive in the years to come. Businesses that use hyperautomation have a bigger chance to remain resilient amidst all the innovations of the digital world. The industry pressure to be faster, more efficient, and more flexible amidst the changing conditions will push businesses to invest in hyperautomation to remain competitive in their field. ‍ The Bottom Line Hyperautomation is one of the most strategic tech trends that businesses can apply today. For hyperautomation to be successful, businesses must identify areas and processes within their operations that need to be automated. The main goal of hyperautomation is to raise the efficiency of business processes. With the use of robotic process automation, machine learning, and artificial intelligence, businesses will be able to leverage hyperautomation and remain competitive in their industry. ‍
